verdict.rationale: Google Cloud ships its own local, in-memory emulators through the gcloud CLI (Firestore is documented) for testing without touching production. They are per-service, do not persist data, and do not enforce all production limits, so they are not a hosted test tenant. Infrastructure Manager preview deployments are a dry-run, not sandbox isolation, and the vendor says the APIs Explorer acts on real data with no sandboxed mode. missing for 10: a hosted sandbox or test tenant spanning services, production-parity limits in the emulators, a sandbox mode for API exploration, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: The Google Cloud CLI provides a local, in-memory emulator for Firestore that you can use to test your application... You should use the emulator only for local testing.
The emulator does not enforce all limits enforced in production
